messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw a regression in prefix cache warmup this morning on a Private cluster. End-to-end p95 token latency +18% for short prompts and KV cache hit rate down to ~42% during steady-state warmups. Seems correlated with netstore tail latencies in the VPC.

ashwin: Details? raw numbers + which clusters?

maria: Private-prod-usw2 (on-prem proxy into S3-compatible blobstore). Quick summary from the perf dump: hosted avg hit-rate 86%, dedicated 78%, private 42%. Warmup period defined as first 60s after a cold session.

kai: Interesting. Could be 2 things interacting: cache key aliasing (we added the `prompt_alias` normalization in 2025-10) + batching heuristic changes that reduced continuous batching windows. If keys aren't normalized the same across proxy and runtime, misses explode.

sofia: I pulled a packet trace — the proxy is doing lowercase-first-token trimming in the VPC-only config (we thought it was benign). That would change the prefix and explain lower hit-rate.

ashwin: Can you paste the config snippet?

sofia: Sure:```yaml
# runtime/cache.yml
key_normalization:
  lowercase: true   # VPC-only override
  trim_leading_spaces: true
  alias_map: /etc/cache/alias.json
```

maria: That matches. Hosted/dedicated use `lowercase: false`. We shipped the VPC override during last-minute hardening and forgot to sync the alias_map semantics.

kai: Kernel/batching angle: because warmup hits dropped, request-level batching falls back to smaller micro-batches -> kernel selection shifts to the lower-throughput kernel (the one optimized for single-stream latency) which increases per-token cost and amplifies p95. I saw the same pattern in a local repro when hit-rate <50%.

ashwin: Do we have profiler traces to show kernel switches?

maria: Yes — attaching a snippet from the profiler (simplified):
```
# sample trace
00:00:10 model:albert_v2 kernel:fast_multi_batch size:32 avg_latency_ms:12
00:00:11 model:albert_v2 kernel:single_stream size:1 avg_latency_ms:28  <-- after cache miss spike
00:00:12 kernel_switch_event: batching window dropped from 12ms -> 3ms
```

sofia: Netstore tail latencies were also higher (TCP retransmits due to VPC firewall rule we tightened). That caused the proxy to return partial responses slower which delayed KV warmups.

maria: TL;DR: three-way failure: (1) config drift (VPC override) changed key normalization, (2) netstore tail increased request latency, (3) batching heuristics + kernel selector reacted and switched kernels -> p95 regression.

kai: Actionable: 1) revert `lowercase: true` in VPC default, 2) add a config sync test for key_normalization across deploy targets, 3) make kernel selector resilient to transient hit-rate drops (grace period before switching kernels), 4) add metric alert for cache hit-rate <65% per-cluster.

ashwin: I agree. I'll own the kernel selector change (will prototype a 5s grace window before switching kernels based on effective batch size).

sofia: I'll roll back the VPC override and add an e2e test — will also add an integration check that verifies `alias_map` loaded and normalized the same in proxy/runtime.

maria: I'll open a short postmortem and run a canary with the revert on a single private cluster. Infra will help monitor.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled by @sofia to private-canary-3 at 2026-03-18T14:05Z. CI checks passed. :rocket:

kai: Also worth adding a small synthetic workload that warms KV with typical prefix distributions so we catch warmup regressions earlier. I can add it to perf harness.

maria: Good call. Assign owners: kernel selector -> @ashwin, config sync + rollback -> @sofia, perf harness warmup -> @kai, postmortem + monitor run -> @maria.

sofia: I'll post PRs shortly. Expect revert PR in ~30m.

ashwin: I'll start a branch for the grace logic and add unit tests for effective_batch_size thresholds.

maria: Thanks all. Will update thread when private-canary metrics are in. :thumbsup:
